context:
Use DuckDB as reference because (a) it's the project's lingua franca and
(b) TPC-H/TPC-DS expected answer sets exist for it. For each benchmark, run
the standard query set on reference + comparison platforms, normalize result
shape (column order per query spec, decimal scale), then diff. Surface
divergences with row/column locator + values.

For tolerances, start strict (exact match) and add per-query overrides only
when a real spec rule (e.g., TPC-H epsilon for floating-point aggregates)
justifies it.

Treat the pytest suite as the canonical execution surface for v1. If a
human-facing CLI becomes desirable later, add it after the comparison
semantics stabilize rather than inventing `benchbox validate-results` up
front.
description:
Quality plan Phase 2b - anchor of the measurement-integrity workstream.
BenchBox's product is trustworthy benchmark results, but the audit found no
centralized correctness validation comparing query results across platforms.
Today, divergent results between (say) DuckDB and ClickHouse on the same
TPC-H query at SF=0.01 would not fail CI.

Build a `core/validation/cross_platform.py` module plus a pytest-based
validation suite. The core comparator should run a benchmark on a reference
platform (DuckDB) and a comparison platform, then assert result-set equality
with per-benchmark tolerances (numeric precision, ordering rules per TPC
spec, NULL handling). Wire the integration suite into a nightly CI matrix
covering DuckDB × {ClickHouse local, DataFusion, Polars-DF} at SF=0.01.

Keep v1 test-first rather than coupling it to a brand-new CLI surface. If
contributors still want a human-facing command after the pytest workflow
proves useful, create that as a follow-up TODO instead of baking it into the
first delivery.

This TODO is also the safety net for the adapter-base refactor
(quality-refactor-adapter-base-into-cohesive-modules).
